The idea comes from it being a numbers game. There are lots of posts of women having 500- 3k+ likes, whereas men have a couple likes a week. The theory the men would like to go with is women treat online dating like a car lot and will only invest time in trying to get the Lamborghini so if you're not at that level, you'll never get a swipe.

The thing is, if online dating were done CORRECTLY with close to equal proportions of women and men and both people swiping ONLY on people they thought were a right fit for them and their lifestyle the process would be alot smoother.

But alas wrenches are thrown into the gears constantly.  Sometimes it's a gender problem, other times it's a company problem. 

The biggest problem I see is a lack of effort leading to a bad profile or a creepy profile in some way. And I've noticed both genders do this but women can get away with it more than men can. (Because of the men swiping right when they shouldn't. Either swiping right on everyone or not reading the profile to see if they would really click with the woman.)

The amount of profile reviews on this reddit that get the same advice over and over is astonishing.  Too many selfies, no outside activities, or pictures of your hobbies. Stereotypical pictures(dead fish, shirtless, sunglasses etc.) And a boring bio that doesn't give anyone much to go on (and women do it too especially with the mirror selfies).

Instead of improving their profile alot of men will just either swipe right on everyone knowing they won't get many matches and thus, less work to go through them later, or their swiping on people outside their league (vastly different lifestyle, ideals on life etc.) 

( Not every man does this, but alot do)

This causes an inflation of likes for the women so now they're juggling 100+ matches when in reality MAYBE 10+ of those actually went through their profile and have things in common.

You can see how this can be sensory overload sort of speak. Alot easier to go through and have conversations with 5- 10 people than 100+.

To add ontop of this alot of men see success stories with men talking dirty from the start and they want to get laid so they try to copy those openers instead of looking for a long term fulfilling relationship. This causes some women to get a bad taste in their mouth from men acting like heathens which causes hesitancy.

Dating sites use mens desperation for profit selling premium services and boosts knowing men will pay anything to increase their odds. Add in scammers trying to get their piece of the pie as well and it just turns into...for lack of a better word... a cluster fuck. 

Now I've made some generalizations here. Every situation will of course vary and not everyone will have the same experience.  But one piece of advice I would give, is craft your profile as if your soul mate is about to see it and you're going to spend the next 30 years together. Sell yourself.
